newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq Jan short interest falls to 1.32 bln shr.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq Jan short interest falls to 1.32 bln shr.

text.p: Nasdaq said January short interest fell to 1.32 billion shares from 1.37 billion shares reported in December.
January's short interest represents 2.38 days of average daily volume, compared to 2.43 days of average daily volume in December, Nasdaq said.
On the Nasdaq National Market, short interest in January totaled 1.27 billion shares, while Nasdaq SmallCap Market securities aggregated 54.7 million shares of short interest, Nasdaq said.
December's short interest totaled 1.31 billion shares on the Nasdaq National Market and 56.1 million shares on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market, Nasdaq said.

A short sale is generally understood to mean the sale of a security that the seller does not own or any sale that is consummated by the delivery of a security borrowed by or for the account of the seller, Nasdaq said. A short sale is often viewed as a bet that a particular stock will decline in price.
Figures this month include all short positions reported December 16, 1996 through January 10, 1997 and settled as of January 15, 1997, Nasdaq said.
